personality: 1 iOS-Native Clean with structural elements of 6 Glass / Luxe
personality_one_liner: A premium, calm, and human interface utilizing Liquid Glass principles to separate functional controls from content, anchored by a warm terracotta palette.

spacing.rule: Generous vertical breathing room. Cards use md/lg padding. UI floats gracefully over content.

icon_set: SF Symbols style fallback to Ionicons (outlined for inactive, filled for active)

do's: Use Liquid Glass (translucent layered surfaces) for the functional layer: tab bars, sticky headers, and floating action containers.
Ensure text on glass is fully readable by applying a tint (>= 70% opacity of surface) behind the blur.
Float the tab bar slightly above the bottom edge if possible, or use a full-width glass bottom bar over scrolling content.
dont's: Do not use glass for text cards or form inputs in the content layer.
Avoid heavy drop shadows; use hierarchy and subtle tinting for depth.

screens.name: Mission Inbox
screens.purpose: A calm, uncrowded home screen displaying new and active missions with distinct visual treatments.

states.loading: Subtle pulsing skeletons matching the card shapes.
states.empty: Warm abstract illustration: 'You're all caught up. We'll notify you when a new mission matches your profile.'
states.error: Readable error message with a soft 'Retry' button.

screens.layout: Header with lightweight name-only greeting ('Good morning, Alex'). Vertical list of large, scannable cards. Standard mission cards use surfaceSecondary. The 'Extra mission' uses a brandTertiary tinted background and a distinct badge to indicate urgency/special request. Cards detail purpose, requested action, estimated duration, and mission type (Text/Voice).

screens.name: Mission Detail - Text
screens.purpose: Structured input screen for written missions, prioritizing the mission context above the questions.
screens.layout: Scrollable content layer. Top: Mission context block. Below: Structured questions with clean text fields. Bottom: Floating sticky glass container housing the 'Submit response' CTA. Follows iOS native generous padding and clear typographic hierarchy.

screens.name: Consent Bottom Sheet
screens.purpose: Explicit, revocable consent capture prior to starting a voice mission.
screens.layout: Triggered via @gorhom/bottom-sheet. Clean typography explaining that voice is recorded to understand *how* the user approaches real work (process). Includes a prominent toggle and a 'Continue' primary button.

screens.name: Mission Detail - Voice
screens.purpose: Immersive, focused call-style interface for audio recording without visual distractions.

states.loading: Connecting state with soft pulsating text.
states.error: Mic permission error with Settings link.

screens.layout: Full-screen interface. Darker or deeply blurred background to signal a mode shift. Top: Mission title and persistent red pulsing recording indicator. Center: Large central VU meter / audio waveform (animated) and a prominent duration timer (e.g., '02:45'). Bottom: Circular native-feeling call controls (Finish, Pause) inside a glass surface.

screens.name: Submission Success
screens.layout: Centered layout. Large checkmark icon (success color), human copy: 'Got it — thank you.', subtext: 'Your response has been securely submitted.' Subtle auto-transition back to Missions or Profile after 2-3 seconds.

screens.name: Capability Profile
screens.purpose: Visual centerpiece displaying observed capabilities (Process vs Outcome) without gamification.

states.empty: Empty state explaining: 'Your profile evolves from how you approach real work. Complete missions to build your capability profile.'

screens.layout: Top: Profile header with abstract fluid background and user avatar. Content: Vertical list of ~5 dimensions (e.g., Domain Intuition, Problem Solving). Each dimension uses an elegant horizontal capability bar. To distinguish contribution: The bar is split. The left/larger segment represents 'Process' (solid brandPrimary). The right/smaller segment represents 'Outcome' (brandTertiary or translucent/striped). Clear typography above the bar labels the dimension. No points, badges, or leaderboards.

screens.name: History
screens.purpose: Secondary tab showing 2-3 believable completed missions.
screens.layout: Simple iOS-native list view. Each row shows mission title, completion date, and a subtle chevron, utilizing the standard layout rhythm. Glass tab bar floats above the scrolling list.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly adhere to the '1 iOS-Native Clean' personality overlaid with 'Liquid Glass' principles. Navigation bars, tab bars, and sticky CTAs should utilize expo-glass-effect (or expo-blur) with proper background tinting to guarantee readability.
Do not use ANY blue, indigo, or purple. The primary accent is a warm Terracotta (#C16E5A).

For the Capability Profile, implement the horizontal capability bars carefully: split a single 100% bar container into two inline segments. The left segment (Process) is larger and uses solid brandPrimary. The right segment (Outcome) uses brandTertiary. Ensure labels are above the bar.

Voice Mission detail must feel like an immersive native call screen. Hide bottom tabs on this screen. Use a persistent red pulsing dot for the recording indicator and display a central audio waveform/VU meter.
The 'Extra mission' card in the inbox needs a distinct visual lift compared to standard missions—use the brandTertiary background color and a specific badge to indicate urgency.
All copy must be human, brief, and conversational (e.g., 'Got it — thank you.'). Avoid point systems, enterprise jargon, or gamified leaderboards entirely.
